Subject: Spike policy & ops qualification — follow-up and next steps

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the team and hear more about Halo Analytics' ingestion and scoring workflows. Quick recap and a few concrete asks so we can size a recommendation: 

Summary of what you shared
- Baseline batch scoring: ~120M tokens/month across training prep and low-cost inference.
- Real-time scoring spikes: up to ~8M tokens/day during campaigns (roughly 3x baseline daily) with short, sharp spikes lasting 30-60 minutes.
- Latency requirement: p95 < 400ms for short text scoring.
- Budget band you mentioned in the call: procurement eyeing $5k to $9k monthly for the initial pilot, flexible if unit economics match.

Clarifying questions / asks for the next step
1) Can you upload the token projection sheet you mentioned (I saw a placeholder in the Slides). If you prefer, send the single-sheet export — we only need daily token buckets and peak windows.
2) Confirm whether the 8M/day spikes are concentrated in a single 1-hour window or spread across multiple smaller bursts. That affects batching and burst policy.
3) Who should be on any procurement threads? I added procurement@haloanalytics.io to CC in case you can confirm a contact.

Preliminary pricing guardrails (to align expectations)
- Target unit economics we can aim for: $60-75 per 1M tokens for mixed traffic under a committed pilot. That translates to roughly $7.2k to $9k/month for the 120M baseline, before spikes.
- Burst handling: we can allow short bursts up to 3x committed rate for up to 15 minutes without immediate throttling. Sustained traffic beyond that will incur overage pricing or trigger a quota increase.
- Overage rate: typically billed by the 1M-token increment. Expect an overage of about $85 per 1M tokens for sustained excess (we can put firm numbers in a formal quote).

Next steps from Redwood
- Once you share the projection sheet I will run a quick simulated cost model and propose two options: a conservative committed bucket (lower unit price, smaller burst cushion) and an elastic option (higher base price but larger burst allowance).
- I'll include a short Mutual Action Plan with timing for pilot start, procurement milestones, and technical onboarding.

I attached a short rate card and will add a clean cost sketch when we have the projection sheet.

Best,

- Budget: procurement gave me latitude up to $10k/mo for a 3-month pilot if we can keep predictable unit pricing.

Subject: Re: Spike policy & ops qualification — follow-up and next steps

Samir — great, thanks for sharing the sheet and introducing Elena. Below are concrete answers and a suggested initial plan so your procurement team can evaluate quickly.

How we handle bursts and overage (summary)
- Aggregation window: we evaluate usage against the committed monthly token bucket on a rolling 24-hour basis for burst detection, and on a calendar-month basis for billing. Short spikes within the burst allowance are not billed as overage.
- Burst allowance: Pilot proposal = 3x committed instantaneous throughput for up to 15 minutes per spike event. You get up to 4 spike events per month under the allowance.
- Overage pricing: If you exceed the burst allowance or the number of allowed spike events, sustained excess is billed at the overage rate of $85 per 1M tokens. This is charged monthly.
- Emergency quota increases: We can process expedited quota increases (target 4 hours) for emergency launches at an additional one-time fee equal to 10% of the estimated incremental monthly spend. Regular quota increases are processed within 48 business hours.

Example cost framing based on your sheet
- Baseline 120M tokens/mo at $70 per 1M -> $8,400/mo.
- If you hit three 8M spike days in a month and exceed the burst cushion, incremental tokens would be billed at $85 per 1M.

Commit / elastic options we will include in the quote
1) Committed pilot: lower unit price ($60-70 per 1M), smaller burst allowance (3x for 15 minutes, 4 events). Best for predictable budgets.
2) Elastic pilot: slightly higher unit price ($75-85 per 1M) with larger burst cushion (5x for 30 minutes, 8 events) and a built-in emergency increase credit.

Next steps I propose
- I will send a short, one-page Mutual Action Plan and a draft SOW by EOD today for your procurement review.
- Marissa, can you prepare a pilot quote for both options above and include DocuSign-ready language for the 48h quota increase and a paid expedited increase?
- Karthik, I'll need one engineering contact from Halo to schedule a 30-minute onboarding call next week to cover sample payloads and latency testing.

If that all sounds good, Elena let us know procurement timing and any redlines you typically require.

Thanks,
